record.system: Anchuri et al. (RandPathTest / lightweight cryptographic proofs of inference)
record.paper_title: Towards Verifiable AI with Lightweight Cryptographic Proofs of Inference
record.technique: Sampling-based spot check. The prover commits to the execution trace with a Merkle-tree vector commitment (SHA-256 row-wise hashes). The Sec. 8 implementation uses a 'hybrid' scheme that commits only the input activation matrix of matmul layers and the output tensor of element-wise layers (Sec. 8.1, p.27). The verifier samples one random output-to-input path (RandPathTest, Fig. 3, p.16). At each path node the prover opens the parents' activations and the edge weights, against the trace commitment Ctrc and a published weight commitment CM (Fig. 4, p.17), and the verifier checks local consistency. The protocol is interactive; a secure non-interactive Fiat-Shamir version is left open (p.29). Appendix D gives a two-server refereed-delegation variant that bisects hashed traces and terminates in O(log T) rounds (p.37-38).
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes, by recomputing in cleartext at the opened positions. Each opened node is checked as a~_j = phi(sum_i w_ij a~_i) from opened parent activations and weights (Fig. 3/4). Element-wise layers are committed as output tensors (Sec. 8.1). The idealized test uses exact equality. The experiments and the App. I parameter procedure use floating-point separation thresholds; there is no finite-field arithmetic. The paper gives no separate treatment of softmax/attention.
record.soundness_error: Statistical/empirical only; there is no negligible cryptographic bound. Other-model soundness error is eps(lambda) <= eps_tst(lambda) + eps_sep (Sec. 5.2, p.16), and trace separation is validated only by experiment. App. I.4 (p.49): 'a soundness error of approximately (eps_sep + eps_tst)', with example targets eps_sep = 0.01 (Alg. 1, p.48) and eps_target = 0.05 (p.49). Single-path detection 'cannot exceed 1/N', where N is the maximum layer width (p.18; repeated p.28). Full soundness for LLMs is left open (p.8, p.18). The authors argue that low per-query soundness is acceptable at scale, for auditing, or with penalties (p.8).
record.trust_assumptions: The weight commitment CM is the agreed ground truth (Fig. 4, p.17). The Merkle/SHA-256 commitment is binding. The verifier's challenge is fresh (interactive protocol). Security rests on the empirical trace-separation property under the other-model or strong other-model soundness adversary (App. H). The scheme is not zero-knowledge: openings reveal activations and weights in the clear (footnote 2, p.3).
record.weights_public: The paper links no code or model release. Llama-2-7b-hf and Llama-2-7b-chat-hf are gated on Hugging Face (manual Llama 2 licence approval; checked via the HF API). The ResNet-18 dogs-vs-cats / dogs-vs-squirrels and dog-breed classifiers are the authors' own fine-tunes and are not released. The datasets are Animals-10 and dogs-cats-images (Kaggle; footnotes 10-11, p.19), Stanford Dogs (footnote 21, p.44) and the Iris toy dataset (scikit-learn; footnote 14, p.24).
record.notes: Page numbers refer to the arXiv v1 PDF. Costs are reported ONLY for Llama-2-7B (Sec. 8); the paper gives no commit, proof or verify cost for ResNet-18. The Sec. 8 trace is '192 intermediate tensors ... each with dimensions of 64 x 4096' (p.27); 64 is not explicitly called the token count. The proof contains 'the relevant row and the corresponding Merkle path for each layer' (p.27). The number of paths per proof is not stated. zkLLM prove/verify timings were run by the authors with the public code (github.com/jvhs0706/zkllm-ccs2024, footnote 15). The zkLLM proof size was 'taken from their paper' (p.27). zkLLM's own Table 1 (CCS'24, arXiv 2404.16109, p.12; A100-40GB, sequence length 2048) reports for LLaMa-2-7B: commit 531 s, prove 620 s, proof 183 kB, verify 2.36 s, 15.5 GB. The 2.36 s is identical to Anchuri's figure, so it may be copied rather than re-measured. The 3.4 MB total proof includes the weights and their Merkle openings ('effectively doubles the payload size', p.28). The intro cites zkLLM at 'around 15 minutes' for up to 13B parameters (p.2). Precision is FP16 for the Llama separation experiments (p.21) and not stated for the Sec. 8 timings.

record.paper_title: TOPLOC: A Locality Sensitive Hashing Scheme for Trustless Verifiable Inference
record.technique: Activation fingerprint (locality-sensitive hash). The provider takes the top-k (k=128) indices and values of the last hidden state every 32 generated tokens, plus one set for the prompt. It encodes them as a polynomial congruence modulo an injective modulus, with 2-byte coefficients (Sec. 4, p.3; Sec. 5.8, p.7). The validator re-runs one prefill over all tokens with the claimed model. It accepts if the exponent-mismatch count, the mean mantissa diff and the median mantissa diff are under thresholds: bf16 Texp=38, Tmean=10, Tmedian=8; fp32 Texp=8, Tmean=256, Tmedian=128 (Sec. 5.2, p.4). Complexity (App. C, p.12): Newton interpolation O(k^2); Horner evaluation O(k); injective-modulus search O(k) with a worst-case constant of 65,536; modular inverse O(log M). The validator's cost is a full prefill of the model.
record.handles_nonlinear: Not applicable. There is no algebraic check; the validator recomputes the full model, so any architecture works (Llama, Intellect-1 and Gemma-2 were tested).
record.soundness_error: Empirical only, with no formal bound. The paper detects modified models, prompts or precision 'with 100% accuracy' and no false positives or negatives in its evaluations (abstract, p.1; Table 6: FPR 0%, FNR 0%/0%). Stated limits: the fp8-vs-bf16 margin is small (Sec. 6.1); speculative decoding cannot be detected (Sec. 6.2); unstable-prompt mining (Sec. 6.3); spoofing last-layer activations (Sec. 6.4); subtle fine-tunes and prompt tweaks are hard to detect (Sec. 6.5).
record.trust_assumptions: A trusted validator holds the correct model and a GPU and re-runs the prefill. Thresholds are calibrated for GPU nondeterminism. There is no cryptographic binding of weights.
record.weights_public: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct are gated (Llama 3.1 licence, manual approval on HF). Gemma-2-9b-it is gated (Gemma terms). INTELLECT-1-Instruct is not gated (Apache-2.0). The UltraChat dataset is public. Llama-2-13B (the Table 6 label) is gated.
record.notes: Table 6 is captioned 'Llama-2-13B', but the Sec. 5 experiments use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, INTELLECT-1-Instruct and Gemma-2-9b-it. The paper does not state where or on what hardware or sequence length the Table 6 TOPLOC and raw-activation numbers were measured. The zkLLM and SVIP columns are quoted from those papers. TOPLOC's zkLLM figures are mislabelled. In zkLLM's own Table 1 (A100-40GB, seq len 2048), for LLaMa-2-13B, 986 s is the committing time, 803 s the prover time and 3.95 s the verifier time; the proof is 188 kB, the commitment 11.0 MB and memory 23.1 GB, all per inference, not per token. SVIP's quote (803 s / 3.95 s) is the consistent one. Robustness hardware is 1xA100, 1x4090 and 2x4090, with Flash / SDPA / Flex attention (Table 2). Default precision is bf16 (7 mantissa bits); fp32 was also tested (Table 5).

record.paper_title: SVIP: Towards Verifiable Inference of Open-source Large Language Models
record.venue_year: arXiv 2410.22307 (v1 Oct 2024; v3 31 Jan 2026, marked 'Preprint'); also on OpenReview (id OaKEGJLhP9)
record.technique: Secret-based hidden-state fingerprint. The provider returns the generated text plus processed hidden states of the prompt. A proxy task maps hidden states to a 128-dim label vector: a 4-layer transformer feature extractor g run by the provider, and an MLP head f plus a task-embedding network t run by the user. A labelling network y(x, s), built from a sentence transformer plus MLPs, generates the target label from the prompt and a 48-bit secret s. The verifier accepts if the L2 distance is at most eta. Secrets rotate after M* queries (typically 400-600); the protocol is retrained after N* secrets. Batch hypothesis testing aggregates per-query outcomes.
record.handles_nonlinear: Not applicable. There is no computation check; it tests model identity through a learned proxy on hidden states.
record.soundness_error: Statistical, with no strict security guarantee (App. B.1, p.12). Per query: FNR below 5% and FPR below 3% (abstract; Table 2). Batch rule, Theorem B.1 (p.13): Pr(Vbar < tau | honest) <= exp(-2B(p1 - tau)^2) and Pr(Vbar >= tau | dishonest) <= exp(-2B(tau - p0)^2). Theorem 3.1 (p.5): B=30 gives both errors below 10^-5 for per-query rates below 5%. Example (Gaussian approximation, App. B.3): B=30, tau=0.5, Llama-3.1-70B vs Llama-2-7B gives type-I 1.7x10^-49 and type-II 0.0 (p.7, p.14). The secret-guess success rate is 1 - delta, e.g. 0.53% for Llama-2-13B (Table 13, p.20).
record.trust_assumptions: A trusted platform or third party trains the labelling network and proxy task and manages secrets. The provider must not obtain the user's secret. Adaptive attacks are bounded only empirically: adapter attack (Fig. 4) and secret recovery (below 50% ASR up to 200,000 pairs, Table 3).
record.code_url: https://github.com/ASTRAL-Group/SVIP (App. A, p.12; the old name SVIP_LLM_Inference_Verification redirects here)
record.weights_public: Specified models: Llama-2-13B (gated, Llama 2 licence), GPT-NeoX-20B (not gated), OPT-30B (not gated), Falcon-40B (not gated), Llama-3.1-70B (gated). Alternative models: GPT2-XL, GPT-NEO-2.7B, GPT-J-6B, OPT-6.7B and Vicuna-7B (open) and Llama-2-7B (gated). Gating was checked via the HF API for the Llama, NeoX, OPT-30B, Falcon-40B and Vicuna-7B-v1.5 entries. LMSYS-Chat-1M requires accepting terms on HF. The web questions, GSM8K and Verifiable-Coding-Problems datasets are also used (App. E.3).

corrections: The technique was described as a 'two-phase bisection'; this is inaccurate. Phase 1 uses multi-level checkpointing: each trainer sends all N checkpoint hashes per level, and the paper explicitly 'eschew[s] the binary search of Canetti et al.' (footnote 2, p.4). Phase 2 sends the full sequence of AugmentedCGNode hashes, checked against the Merkle root, and the referee takes the first differing index (Alg. 2, p.5). Neither phase is binary bisection.
The referee re-executes an operator only in Case 3 (differing output tensor hash). Cases 1-2 are resolved by structure checks or Merkle membership proofs (Sec. 2.3, p.5-6).

record.paper_title: Verde: Verification via Refereed Delegation for Machine Learning Programs
record.venue_year: arXiv 2502.19405v1, 26 Feb 2025 (preprint; Gensyn AI / NYU / a16z crypto research)
record.technique: Refereed delegation / dispute resolution. The client sends the same program to k >= 2 providers. If outputs differ, a two-phase narrowing over hashed state runs. Phase 1 finds the first diverging training/inference step with multi-level checkpointing: N checkpoint hashes per level, recursing into the diverging interval, without binary search (Alg. 1, p.3; footnote 2, p.4). Phase 2 finds the first diverging operator by comparing the full sequences of AugmentedCGNode hashes, which are Merkle-committed as the checkpoint (Alg. 2, p.5). The referee then resolves by graph-structure check, Merkle membership proof, or re-executing one operator (Sec. 2.3). RepOps provides bitwise-reproducible CUDA operators with a fixed floating-point reduction order.
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes. The referee recomputes the single disputed operator natively (or decomposes it further). RepOps covers all operators needed for DistilBERT and the Llama family, in FP32 only (p.2, p.7).
record.soundness_error: Deterministic, conditional on hash collision-resistance and bitwise reproducibility. If at least one provider is honest, their output is accepted (Sec. 2, p.3). If all are dishonest, k-1 are still identified but a wrong output may be accepted. There is no probabilistic sampling error.
record.trust_assumptions: At least one honest provider among k. A neutral, computationally limited referee. A collision-resistant hash (e.g. SHA-256) and Merkle commitments. Bitwise reproducibility across hardware via RepOps (IEEE-754 FP32, single GPU per setup; p.6).

record.paper_title: TAO: Tolerance-Aware Optimistic Verification for Floating-Point Neural Networks
record.technique: Optimistic verification with a Merkle-anchored, threshold-guided interactive dispute game. The game recursively partitions the traced PyTorch graph N ways down to a single operator. At the leaf, the operator is judged against IEEE-754 theoretical bounds (deterministic or probabilistic) or against empirical percentile thresholds calibrated across GPUs. The empirical option is adjudicated by a small honest-majority committee vote. Coordination runs on an Ethereum (Holesky testnet) contract.

record.soundness_error: Empirical plus crypto-economic. With empirical thresholds, ASR is 0.0% for all models even when loosened 3x, with 0% false positives (p.4, Table 2 p.9). With theoretical bounds only, the probabilistic bound allows up to 2.4% ASR on Qwen3-8B (x1) and the deterministic bound up to 12.6% (Qwen3-8B) and 58.6% (BERT-large). ResNet-152 has 0.0% ASR under all bounds. Dispute rounds are ~O(log_N |V|) (Fig. 8 caption, p.13).
record.trust_assumptions: At least one honest challenger within the challenge window. An honest-majority committee at the leaf when empirical thresholds are used. A smart-contract coordinator. record.paper_title: Seal, Then Sample: Sampled Layerwise Proofs for Verifiable LLM Inference from GPT-2 to 70B
record.technique: A hybrid of sampling and SNARKs. The prover commits to the boundary activations of every chunk (2L+3 chunks for L blocks: 47 for TinyLlama, 163 for Llama-2-70B; p.4). Commitments use HyperKZG over BN254 with a Blake3 transcript, and all of them are absorbed before any challenge is drawn. The prover then proves a random subset of candidate chunks plus the input/output anchor chunks. Linear layers use GKR-style sumcheck; nonlinear ones use LogUp-family lookups (p.3). The system is built on a modified deep-prove checkout (Gailly et al., 2026). A packed-batch mode uses a block-diagonal causal mask. The proven object is a fixed-point canonical model.
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes, via LogUp-family lookup arguments. LayerNorm/RMSNorm gadgets admit an approximation range with explicit error bounds (Sec. 8.2).
record.soundness_error: Per audit, a false manifest is accepted with probability <= q(M,b,s) + eps_backend, where q = C(M-b,s)/C(M,s) (Sec. 3.3, p.4). The 70B run (M=161, s=3, b=1) gives coverage 3/161 = 1.863%. Cumulative detection is 1-(1-p)^k: 37 audits for 50%, 160 for 95% (p.5). With a manifest-only Fiat-Shamir schedule, grinding costs ~12.5 ms per attempt on GPT-2 (p.9), so an externally ordered challenge is required.
record.trust_assumptions: Binding commitments and a sound backend. All measurements use a locally generated test reference string (insecure against its generator). An authenticated registry/config and an external, unpredictable challenge (beacon) with enforced ordering and unique accepted manifests are required. No zero-knowledge claim is made (p.2).

record.paper_title: SafetyNets: Verifiable Execution of Deep Neural Networks on an Untrusted Cloud
record.technique: NOT Freivalds. It is an interactive proof: Thaler's (CRYPTO'13) sum-check IP for matrix multiplication plus a new sum-check IP for quadratic activations, in a GKR-style layer-by-layer reduction over F_p (multilinear extensions), batched over b inputs. Stated complexity (Sec 3.1-3.2, pp.5-6): matmul layer i prover O(n_i(n_{i-1}+b)), verifier O(n_i n_{i-1}), 4 log(n_i) field elements exchanged; quadratic-activation layer prover O(b n_i), verifier O(log(b n_i)), 5 log(b n_i) field elements.
record.handles_nonlinear: Only polynomial operations are proved: element-wise quadratic activation (x^2) and sum pooling. ReLU, sigmoid and softmax are allowed only in the final output layer, where the prover sends z_{L-1} and the client computes the output activation itself. Max pooling and stochastic pooling are not supported at all.
record.soundness_error: Lemma 3.1 (p.6): eps = 3b * sum_{i=0}^{L} n_i / p. Paper: 'with p = 2^61 - 1 the soundness error < 1/2^30 for practical network parameters and batch sizes'. Sec 4.3: in all settings eps < 1/2^30. This is statistical (information-theoretic) soundness for an interactive protocol.
record.trust_assumptions: No trusted hardware. Interactive public-coin IP with the client as verifier. Weights are known to both parties, and the verifier evaluates the weight MLE locally. There are no commitments and no model privacy. Only arithmetic-circuit networks (quadratic activations) are supported.
record.weights_public: No trained weights in the repo (files: sn.cc, timit_arch.txt, Makefile, README, LICENSE). Its README says CNNs must first be converted to fully connected equivalents. MNIST and MNIST-Back-Rand (Montreal MNIST variations page) are public. TIMIT is distributed by the LDC under licence and is not a free download.

record.paper_title: Slalom: Fast, Verifiable and Private Execution of Neural Networks in Trusted Hardware
record.technique: An Intel SGX TEE outsources every linear layer (FC, conv, depthwise/pointwise conv) to an untrusted co-located GPU and checks each result with Freivalds' algorithm over Z_p. The paper uses three variants: (a) on-the-fly Freivalds, (b) batched Freivalds, and (c) Freivalds with preprocessing, where the secret s and s~ = W s are precomputed so each check costs |x|+|y| multiplications. Privacy comes from additive stream-cipher blinding with precomputed unblinding factors. Complexity: Table 2 (p.6), e.g. FC batched verification B(|x|+|y|)+cost_f and with preprocessing B(|x|+|y|). A plain Freivalds check costs 3n^2 multiplications (Lemma 2.1, p.4).
record.handles_nonlinear: Non-linearities (ReLU, pooling, residual merges) are computed directly inside the trusted enclave and are not cryptographically verified. ResNets are handled by verifying the linear layers in both residual paths and computing the activation in the TEE.
record.soundness_error: Theorem 3.2 (p.6): t-integrity with t = n/|S|^k - negl(lambda) for an n-layer DNN and k Freivalds repetitions per layer. Implementation (Sec 4.1, p.7): p = 2^24 - 3, k = 2, S = [-2^19, 2^19], '40 bits of statistical soundness per layer'. For a 50-layer DNN, the chance of fooling the TEE is 'less than 1 in 22 billion'.
record.trust_assumptions: The TEE (Intel SGX enclave) is trusted: it is the verifier, holds the model and the secret Freivalds randomness (designated verifier, s reused across layers), and attests to remote clients. The GPU/host is untrusted. Privacy relies on a secure PRNG (AES-CTR/GCM). The paper notes SGX side-channel caveats. Offline preprocessing is needed for the preproc/privacy modes.
record.weights_public: Pretrained VGG16, MobileNet and ResNet50 are the public Keras ImageNet weights (paper Appendix E; downloadable without an account). ResNet-18/34/101/152 throughput was measured on untrained models. Accuracy is measured on the ImageNet validation set, which requires registration on image-net.org. The repo README warns it is a proof-of-concept for performance testing only and says nothing about weight sourcing.
record.notes: ResNet-18 is benchmarked, but untrained, in SGX, and only throughput is reported. There are no dogs-vs-cats binary models and no LLMs. Most per-model numbers exist only as bar labels in Figures 2-6, read from the PDF and marked 'figure bar labels'. Small text-vs-figure discrepancies: the text says VGG16 'up to a 20.3x increase' while the Figure 3 bar reads 19.8; the text says fused MobileNet 6.4x while the bar reads 6.3; the text says VGG16 privacy-only 13.0x while the bar reads 12.7; the text says privacy+integrity 10.7x while the bar reads 10.4. The ResNet privacy+integrity numbers use 'a preliminary implementation ... without properly constructed unblinding factors' (p.9). Communication is high (over 50MB per inference for VGG16, Sec 2.3, p.4), so the TEE and GPU must be co-located. Table 1 (p.3) gives relative throughput: SafetyNets ≤1/200x, Gazelle ≤1/1000x, the TEE baseline 1x, an insecure GPU ≥50x, and Slalom 4x-20x.

record.paper_title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
record.technique: Sparse Freivalds combined with a linear error-correcting code (RAA codes, rate 1/8, target relative distance 1/2). Transparent preprocessing Q = G^T M. The client samples a t-sparse challenge e and checks (e^T Q)x = e^T(G^T y). Batch verification (Protocol 2) delegates the stacked projections Q_b^T e to the server and checks them with a second coded check. Privacy uses dual-LPN pseudorandom masks x' = G_x e_x with a preprocessed P = M G_x. Complexity: client online O(N + l*t*n) per MVM (Table 1, p.8), O_kappa(m+n) overall. Preprocessing O(mn). Batch client O(BN + B l(n+t) + l' t' B n + l l'(Bn + t t')) (pp.8-9). In the base protocol the honest server performs only the ordinary MVM. Batch verification adds one round and O(B l t n) server field operations, returning B l n field elements (p.9).
record.handles_nonlinear: Nonlinear operations are not verified cryptographically. The client evaluates them locally, which the paper says is <1% of inference time (p.2). In verification-only mode the server runs the whole model and the client replays the nonlinear operations locally from the returned y_j to reconstruct each x_j before batch-checking M_j x_j = y_j.
record.soundness_error: Information-theoretic. Each repetition accepts a wrong y with probability <= (1-delta)^t + 1/(|F|-1) (Lemma 5.1, p.7). With l repetitions the soundness error is <= 2^-kappa (Theorem 5.2, pp.7-8), plus p_fail of the sampled code (Remark 5.3, p.8). Batch verification: eps^l + (eps')^l' (Theorem 5.4, p.8). Parameters: kappa = 40 (statistical), lambda = 128 (computational, privacy); BabyBear field q = 15*2^27 + 1; t_y = 31, l = 2; t_x = 160..154 for n = 2^10..2^14.
record.trust_assumptions: No TEE and no trusted setup. The model is public; preprocessing is transparent, and anyone can check Q. Soundness is information-theoretic against an unbounded server. Input privacy is computational under dual-LPN (RAA codes assumed 'plausibly dual-LPN-friendly'). The protocol is interactive (182 rounds in standard/boost mode, 1 round in verification-only mode).
record.weights_public: Qwen3-4B is an open-weight model on Hugging Face (Qwen/Qwen3-4B and Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8 are not gated, Apache-2.0). The paper runs FP8-stored weights re-quantized as round(2^8 W). No code repository is given in the paper.
record.notes: Closest in spirit to our defence (Freivalds plus a linear code). The main difference is that Maverick's code is used only to make a sparse challenge sound, with no commitment. It benchmarks Qwen3-4B, not Llama-2-7B or ResNet-18. Maverick quotes DeepProve for context (p.15, not measured by Maverick): GPT-2 34.2 s prove / 1.35 s verify, Gemma 3 81.6 s / 1.91 s on an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D, proofs 9-43 MiB. Communication (p.15): standard/boost modes send 21.83 MB and receive 36.00 MB (57.83 MB total, 182 rounds); verification-only sends 81.92 kB and receives 36.00 MB (36.08 MB, single round). Table 6 (p.14) lists per-block Qwen3-4B linear shapes (in -> out): q_proj 2560->4096, k/v_proj 2560->1024, o_proj 4096->2560, gate/up 2560->9728, down 9728->2560. The table exponents 2^k appear as '2k' in the PDF text and are written here as 2^k. Table 5 end-to-end = server total + client online (e.g. 392.26 + 29.68 = 421.94 ms at n = 2^12).

record.paper_title: LAMP: Linear Verification of Matrix Multiplication via Proximity Testing
record.technique: A commit-and-prove SNARK for a single k x k product AB = C. It combines Freivalds' check (structured challenge r = (1, r, ..., r^{k-1})) with proximity testing over a linear code (Reed-Solomon, rate 1/2). The prover commits to row-wise encoded A, B, C (Pedersen leaves in a Merkle tree) and to encoded intermediates x = rA, y = xB, z = rC. The Groth16 CP-SNARK then checks only t sampled encoded-column fold equations and the RS code-consistency of x, y, z. Merkle openings and QA-NIZK CP-Link bind the in-circuit values to the commitments. Complexity (Table 1, p.9): circuit O(tk + E_code) constraints, linear in k for fixed t. Prover O(3nk) group ops + O(n) hashes for the ABC commit and O(k^2) field ops for the intermediates. Verifier E^V_snark + O(t log n) hashes + E^V_link (O(t) pairing terms). Parameters: t = 128, RS rate 1/2.
record.handles_nonlinear: No. It proves only matrix-multiplication statements. The GPT-2 workload covers only the matmuls of one layer; the README says LayerNorm, activation functions, softmax, tokenization and language-model inference are outside the benchmark scope.
record.soundness_error: Theorem 6.2 (p.11), interactive computational soundness: Pr[Acc] <= eps_cp + eps_open + eps_link + eps_code + (k-1)/|F| + 4(1-delta)^t. Here eps_code <= 3(n-1)/(|F|-n) for the RS check (Definition 6.1). Implementation: t = 128 sampled positions, RS rate 1/2, BN254 scalar field. The Fiat-Shamir variant adds the random-oracle loss (Remark 3).
record.trust_assumptions: Groth16 CP-SNARK over BN254 (circuit-specific trusted setup, pairings). Pedersen commitments (discrete log) and collision-resistant Merkle hashing. QA-NIZK CP-Link. Fiat-Shamir in the ROM for the non-interactive version. Zero-knowledge (Pedersen hiding) keeps the matrices private.
record.weights_public: No model weights are needed. Only matmul shapes are benchmarked, and the repo includes no weights or datasets. The repo README says the GPT-2 dimensions 'are fixed to GPT-2 medium' (D = 1024, 16 heads, Dh = 64, MLP M = 4096); the paper says only 'a single GPT-2 layer with sequence length 2^10'. GPT-2 weights are public.
record.notes: Design-wise, the closest published system to our defence (Freivalds + RS code + Merkle commitment). It differs in wrapping the check in Groth16 and in handling no ReLU or other nonlinearity. It does not benchmark ResNet-18 or Llama-2-7B. The Introduction (p.2) says the GPT-2 proving time drops 1.78x, while Sec 7.4 and the conclusion say 1.77x; the abstract does not mention GPT-2. In Table 2 the Freivalds-baseline proof size is printed once (196 B, a Groth16 proof) and is blank for the other rows. At k = 2^13 the Freivalds baseline runs out of memory. record.technique: An optimizing compiler from TFLite to halo2 ZK-SNARK circuits, with gadget selection and layout optimisation. record.system: TwinShield [extra: random-linear-combination (hash-row) integrity for TEE+GPU; benchmarks LLaMA-7B]
record.paper_title: Securing Transformer-based AI Execution via Unified TEEs and Crypto-protected Accelerators
record.venue_year: arXiv 2507.03278v2 (2025); also an OpenReview submission titled 'TwinShield: Secure Foundation Model Execution by Unifying TEEs and Crypto-protected Accelerators'
record.technique: An SGX TEE offloads linear layers, attention matmuls (OutAttnMult) and the exponentiations of SoftMax (OutSoftMax) to an untrusted GPU. Integrity uses 'U-Verify': the TEE samples a secret random vector h and appends the hash row hash_A = h*A to A. The GPU computes the augmented product, and the TEE checks h*C = hash_A*B, a Freivalds-style check with 2 instead of 3 vector-matrix products. Softmax exponentiation is checked multiplicatively with secret random integer coefficients a_i: prod(e^{x_i})^{a_i} = e^{hash_X}. Stated complexity (Sec V, pp.8-9): the TEE hash costs n*m multiplications, the GPU (m+1)*n*p, and TEE verification m*p. Softmax verification needs up to n(a_max - 1) + n multiplications. Quantization follows Slalom/DarKnight.
record.handles_nonlinear: SoftMax exponentiation is outsourced and verified with the U-Verify random-coefficient product check (secret coefficients); SoftMax additions and divisions stay in the TEE. LayerNorm, GeLU and ReLU stay inside the TEE and are trusted, not verified (<5% of execution time per the paper).
record.soundness_error: Stated as 'security levels', not a formal soundness theorem. U-Verify for OutSoftMax: attack success rate limited to 1/(n*2^d), security level log(n*2^d), raised with OutSoftMax masking to log(n*2^d*d^n) (p.8). OutAttnMult privacy level log(d*(2m)!), where d is the field size, e.g. 'approximately 13,471 bits' for BERT (p.6). Field Z_p with p = 2^24 - 3.
record.trust_assumptions: Trusted Intel SGX enclave (verifier; holds the secret hash vectors, coefficients and masks). The GPU/accelerator is untrusted. Designated-verifier: the secrets must stay hidden from the GPU. One-time use of scalars/masks prevents replay.
record.weights_public: The paper says it 'acquired a pre-trained, quantized 8-bit LLaMA model from HuggingFace' without naming the repo. Original LLaMA-7B weights were released by Meta on request, so they are gated. ViT, BERT and CLIP come from Keras. ImageNet needs registration; SST-2 and WikiText are public.

record.system: VeriAttn (CTGA) [extra: Gaussian-variant Freivalds for LLM attention in TEE+GPU; compares against zkLLM]
record.paper_title: Communication-Efficient Verifiable Attention for LLM Inference
record.technique: TEE-shielded partitioning (Intel TDX) that offloads both the linear and the non-linear attention steps to an untrusted GPU. GVFAVeriMM uses the Gaussian variant of Freivalds (secret Gaussian vector w_G, tolerance eps calibrated on honest FP16 GPU runs) to check value aggregation. LPVeriExp uses a log-product random-integer-coefficient check for the softmax exponentiation. Two-level prefill pipelining and TEE-GPU collaborative decoding when the KV cache exceeds GPU memory. Stated verification complexity: prefill O(L^2 + L d_h) instead of O(L^2 d_h); decoding O(t + d_h) per step with an incrementally maintained projection.
record.handles_nonlinear: Exponentiation in softmax is verified with LPVeriExp (log-product residual with tolerance eps'). Other components (projection and feed-forward layers) follow TSDP, i.e. linear parts offloaded and verified, non-linear parts in the TEE. The whole scheme is tolerance-based floating point, not exact field arithmetic.
record.soundness_error: Statistical and tolerance-based. Lemma 1: Pr[||(C-AB)w_G||_inf <= eps | C != AB] <= 2*Phi(eps/sigma) - 1 per repetition, (2*Phi(eps/sigma) - 1)^tau over tau repetitions. Lemma 2 (LPVeriExp): Pr[FA_r] <= 1{n_err >= 2}/N_a + (2*Phi(eps'/sigma') - 1)^(tau_g*tau_a). Deviations within the tolerance budget are accepted by design. The experiments use 10 repetitions with tolerance set to 2x the largest clean residual. Empirically 1,000/1,000 injected faults were detected with 0/1,000 false rejections.
record.trust_assumptions: A trusted Intel TDX CPU TEE acts as verifier and keeps the Gaussian vectors and coefficients secret from the GPU (designated verifier). The GPU is untrusted. Accepted outputs may deviate within the calibrated numerical budget. The paper does not address confidentiality, and side-channel and DoS attacks are out of scope.
record.weights_public: LLaMA3-3B (Llama 3.2) and LLaMA3-8B are gated on Hugging Face and need Meta licence acceptance. Qwen3-14B (Apache-2.0) and Phi-4-14B (MIT) are openly downloadable. WikiText is public.
record.notes: Included as the closest Freivalds-family LLM system that reports a head-to-head against zkLLM, but the model is LLaMA3-8B, not Llama-2-7B. The zkLLM comparison (Figures 9 and 14, pp.10-11) is given only as log-scale plots and the text 'roughly two orders of magnitude higher latency'; no per-point numbers are labelled. record.paper_title: zkCNN: Zero Knowledge Proofs for Convolutional Neural Network Predictions and Accuracy
record.technique: GKR/sumcheck interactive proof, made non-interactive with Fiat-Shamir in the random oracle model. New linear-time sumcheck for FFT: prover O(M+N), proof and verifier O(log N). 2-D convolution is proven as FFT -> Hadamard product -> IFFT (three sumchecks): prover O(n^2), proof O(log n), or O(log^2 n) proof and verifier in the variant with delegated verifier computation. FC layers use Thaler's matrix-multiplication sumcheck [41]. Generalised GKR gates take inputs from any layer. Weights and auxiliary witness are committed with the Hyrax/Spartan polynomial commitment [39,44] on BLS12-381 (prover O(N), proof and verifier O(sqrt N)).
record.handles_nonlinear: ReLU: a negative x is encoded as p-|x|. The prover supplies the bit decomposition (b_0..b_{Q-1}) of |x| plus a sign bit b_Q (0 negative, 1 positive). The circuit checks that the bits are binary and recompose correctly, then outputs b_Q times the top Q' bits (truncation). Max pooling is fused with ReLU: the prover supplies x_max, each x_max - x_j is bit-decomposed (Q bits, no sign bit), the circuit checks x_max * prod_j(x_max - x_j) = 0, and x_max's own bits are validated. Compared with ReLU alone, that is one extra bit decomposition. Average pooling is supported. Quantisation rescaling by 2^-E uses bit decomposition and shift.
record.soundness_error: GKR soundness O(d log|C|/|F|) (Theorem A.1, p.15, citing Libra [48]), where d is circuit depth. The field comes from Curve BLS12-381, which 'offers 128-bits of security' (p.11). Fiat-Shamir 'only incurs a negligible soundness loss' (p.11). The polynomial commitment relies on discrete log. No concrete numeric soundness error is given for the full system.
record.trust_assumptions: Transparent: no trusted setup or CRS (the paper contrasts this with the tens-of-GB CRSs of vCNN/ZEN). Discrete-log assumption for the polynomial commitment; random oracle for Fiat-Shamir. The ZK variant is described but its 'formal protocol and the proof' are omitted. The code README says 'Currently this version doesn't add complete zero-knowledge property.'
record.weights_public: Code is public (MIT). The repo ships data.tar.gz with demo folders data/lenet5.mnist.relu.max/ and data/vgg11/. record.paper_title: pvCNN: Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Convolutional Neural Network Testing
record.venue_year: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security, vol. 18, 2023, pp. 2218-2233 (arXiv 2201.09186)
record.technique: The CNN is split into a private PriorNet, which the model developer evaluates on HE-encrypted test data (Microsoft SEAL; dc=4096, q=2^109, t=1032193), and a public LaterNet. Correctness is proven with Groth16 zk-SNARKs (libsnark). Convolution and FC are expressed as a single matrix multiplication via a one-degree Quadratic Matrix Program (QMP); ReLU and pooling use QAP circuits. Layers are glued with LegoSNARK-style commit-and-prove, and proofs from multiple testers are aggregated. The paper's Table I gives proving complexity O(Mn^2 · Mn^2), versus O(M·Mn^2·(n^2+m^2)) for vCNN and zkCNN.
record.handles_nonlinear: ReLU and pooling are QAP-based: 'a ReLU operation needs 20 constraints and an average pooling operation needs 144 constraints'. The circuits use average pooling; the paper also mentions expressing max pooling as QAP.
record.soundness_error: Partly quantified. For each PriorNet layer, the random-point polynomial identity check fails with probability dc/q = 4096/2^109, with the point k from a random-oracle HASH (Sec. VI, p.13). The rest relies on the knowledge soundness of the commit-and-prove zk-SNARKs (Groth16/LegoSNARK-based), which is not quantified numerically. Privacy relies on semantic security of the leveled FHE.
record.trust_assumptions: Trusted setup (Groth16 CRS, very large for QMP: up to 16,927,629,296 KB as reported in Table V), pairing assumptions, random oracle for HASH, FHE semantic security.

record.paper_title: Mystique: Efficient Conversions for Zero-Knowledge Proofs with Applications to Machine Learning
record.technique: Interactive, designated-verifier ZK based on subfield VOLE (LPN-based sVOLE, Quicksilver [YSWW21]) over F_p with p = 2^61 - 1. It adds efficient arithmetic-to-Boolean conversions (zk-edaBits), conversions from publicly committed to authenticated values (C2A, via a PRF in a Boolean circuit and a Merkle-tree commitment), and fixed-point/floating-point conversions. The matrix-multiplication proof generalises Freivalds' algorithm: an n x n matmul costs n private multiplications instead of n^3, using random vectors u, v over an extension field F_{q^k} and a CheckZero step. It is integrated into the Rosetta (TensorFlow) framework.
record.handles_nonlinear: ReLU, max pooling, sigmoid, SoftMax and batch normalisation use arithmetic-Boolean conversions (edaBits) and Boolean circuits. IEEE-754 single-precision float circuits (from EMP) with Fix2Float/Float2Fix conversions. Fixed-point encoding uses a 30-bit range with s = 16 fractional bits.
record.soundness_error: 'computational security parameter λ = 128 and statistical security parameter ρ ≥ 40' (p.22). The MatMul protocol has 'soundness error 3/q^k' (Theorem 5, p.18). The edaBits check reaches 'at least 40-bit statistical security' for N = 10^6 (B = 3, c = 2) (p.12). The field is F_p with p = 2^61 - 1.

record.paper_title: ZENO: A Type-based Optimization Framework for Zero Knowledge Neural Network Inference
record.technique: Optimising framework for zkSNARK NN inference, benchmarked against and built on arkworks (Groth16, cited for 192-byte proofs). It keeps tensor and privacy type information to reduce R1CS work. The ZENO circuit IR makes a dot product O(n) instead of O(n^2) computation, and this extends to FC, conv and pool. 'Knit encoding' packs 8-bit values into 254-bit field elements when only one side (weights or features) is private. It adds a workload-specialised parallel scheduler, constraint-system sharing across a batch of images, and zkSNARK-aware fusion of injective layers (e.g. BN/scale) into conv/FC.
record.handles_nonlinear: ReLU via comparison: the 'circuit first decomposes an integer into n(=254) bits and checks whether the first bit equals zero' (p.4); 'relu requires expensive comparison operator with hundreds of constraints' (p.10), so it is not fused. Average pooling is a dot product with a ones vector. Injective layers such as batch normalisation are fused into the preceding linear layers.
record.soundness_error: Not quantified. It inherits zkSNARK (Groth16 via arkworks) security. The field is '≈2^254 in case of BLS12-381' (p.2), and the text refers to 254-bit finite fields.
record.trust_assumptions: Groth16-style per-circuit trusted setup (arkworks backend).

record.paper_title: ZKML: An Optimizing System for ML Inference in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
record.technique: Optimising compiler from ML models (tflite) to halo2 (Plonkish) circuits. A cost-model optimizer chooses among gadget implementations and physical layouts (columns and rows), using fixed-point arithmetic with lookup-table gadgets. Two backends: KZG (universal trusted setup) and IPA (transparent).
record.handles_nonlinear: Fixed-point with a ZKML-chosen scale factor. Pointwise non-linearities other than ReLU (ELU, sigmoid, exp, tanh) use lookup tables. ReLU can be done by bit decomposition (no lookups, b+2 cells, the zkCNN approach) or by a 2-cell lookup into an (x, ReLU(x)) table; ZKML's layout uses the lookup, and the optimizer picks gadgets. Max uses (c-a)(c-b)=0 plus two range lookups. Softmax uses exp lookups after subtracting the max.
record.soundness_error: Not quantified. It 'inherits all security properties of halo2, including zero-knowledge, completeness, and knowledge soundness'.
record.trust_assumptions: KZG: one-time universal trusted setup (Privacy Scaling Explorations ceremony for 2^28 'with over 75 participants'). IPA: transparent, but with larger proofs and slower verification.
record.weights_public: Code is public (Apache-2.0). The examples/ folder contains mnist, nlp, train_graph, twitter and v2_1.0_224_truncated (MobileNet v2). No ResNet-18 or VGG16 CIFAR-10 model files were seen in examples/. CIFAR-10 is public. ImageNet download requires registration, but MobileNet v2 weights are public (TF). The distilled GPT-2 is public on Hugging Face.
record.notes: Hardware: r6i.8xlarge (32 vCPU cores/threads, 256 GB RAM) for all models except MobileNet (r6i.16xlarge, 64 vCPU, 512 GB) and GPT-2/Diffusion (r6i.32xlarge, 128 vCPU, 1 TB). ZKML's ResNet-18 (CIFAR-10) has only 280.9K parameters (81.9M flops), far smaller than a standard ResNet-18 (~11M params), so matching it requires the same reduced model. Table 9 lists ZKML VGG-16 at 584.1 s / 16 ms, versus 637.14 s / 9.62 ms in Table 6, and ResNet-18 proof at 15.3 kB versus 15744 bytes in Table 6. The paper does not explain these differences beyond saying hardware was matched to prior work 'as closely as possible' (ResNet-18 prove time is identical in both). record.paper_title: ZKML: An Optimizing System for ML Inference in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
record.technique: Compiles TFLite models into halo2 (Plonkish) ZK-SNARK circuits. It uses gadgets for shape, arithmetic, pointwise non-linearities and specialised ops, plus a cost-model optimizer that picks gadgets and the circuit layout (columns and rows). Backend is KZG or IPA. Values are fixed-point with a scale factor that ZKML chooses.
record.handles_nonlinear: Pointwise non-linearities (ReLU, exp and others) use lookup tables. Bit decomposition over arithmetic rows is an alternative the optimizer weighs (Sec 3 toy example, 16-bit ReLU). Max uses lookups, and variable division and scaled exponentiation have their own gadgets. Softmax and BatchMatMul are supported (Table 3).
record.soundness_error: Not quantified. Sec 4.3 (p.5) says 'ZKML inherits all of the assumptions and security properties of the underlying proving system', i.e. halo2 knowledge soundness and zero-knowledge. No bit-security figure is given.
record.trust_assumptions: KZG needs a one-time universal trusted setup. The paper uses the Privacy Scaling Explorations ceremony for 2^28 (>75 participants, p.5). IPA needs no trusted setup and 'usually' has larger proofs and slower verification. The weights are private (knowledge soundness means the prover knows the input and weights).
record.weights_public: Only partially. The repo's examples/ has mnist (model.tflite plus msgpack files, public), nlp, train_graph, twitter and v2_1.0_224_truncated. The ResNet-18/VGG-16 CIFAR-10 weights are not confirmed in the repo. 7 of ZKML's 8 models (mnist, resnet, dlrm, mobilenet, vgg, gpt2, diffusion; Twitter excluded) are distributed as msgpack (360MB) by the Artemis authors: 'aws s3 sync s3://pps-artemis-artifacts/models examples/models' (github.com/pps-lab/artemis README; the README does not say whether AWS credentials are needed). None are gated.
record.notes: Hardware (Sec 9.1, p.11): AWS r6i.8xlarge (32 vCPU threads, 256 GB) for all models except MobileNet (r6i.16xlarge, 64 vCPU, 512 GB), and GPT-2 and Diffusion (r6i.32xlarge, 128 vCPU, 1 TB). Model sizes are in Table 5 (p.10). 'ResNet-18 (CIFAR-10)' has only 280.9K params and 81.9M FLOPs, far smaller than the standard 11M-param ResNet-18. VGG16 (CIFAR-10) has 15.2M params. GPT-2 is a distilled GPT-2 with 81.3M params. MobileNet v2 is the 1.0/224 ImageNet version with 3.5M params. MNIST is an 8.1K-param CNN. Table 9 (p.12) quotes prior work as reported: zkCNN VGG-16 90.3% / 88.3 s / 59 ms / 341 kB, and vCNN 90.4%* / 31 hours* / 20 seconds / 0.34 kB (the vCNN prove time was estimated by zkCNN's authors). record.paper_title: ZKTorch: Compiling ML Inference to Zero-Knowledge Proofs via Parallel Proof Accumulation
record.technique: Compiles ONNX models, via a transpiler and graph-rewriting compiler, into a DAG of 'basic blocks' such as CQ/CQLin lookups, matmul and additions. Each block is proved with a specialised KZG-based Poly-IOP, and the many per-block proofs are folded with a parallel extension of the Mira pairing-based accumulation scheme. It runs over BN254 and supports 61 layer types.
record.handles_nonlinear: Lookup basic blocks (CQ). For example, GeLU (4 Mul, 1 Pow, 1 Tanh in ONNX) is fused into one CQ lookup, and nonlinearities are combined wherever possible (Sec 5). Rescaling after CQLin uses CQ.
record.soundness_error: Union bound over DAG nodes. 'we have at most 100,000 nodes in our DAG, so we can achieve a total soundness error of e by setting the threshold of each individual node at 1/(10^6) e'. The paper adds that 'due to our field size, this error is negligible' (Sec 4.3, p.6). Knowledge soundness is argued in the AGM (Appendix B/C).
record.trust_assumptions: KZG polynomial commitments on the pairing-friendly curve BN254 over a 254-bit prime field, which needs an SRS. Security is argued in the AGM with Fiat-Shamir. The weights stay hidden from the verifier.
record.code_url: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/zkt-2477 (cited in paper Appendix A); public repo https://github.com/uiuc-kang-lab/zk-torch (Apache-2.0; not cited in paper)

record.paper_title: zkPyTorch: A Hierarchical Optimized Compiler for Zero-Knowledge Machine Learning
record.technique: A PyTorch-to-ONNX preprocessor builds a DAG with extra auxiliary nodes (for example, a division remainder). ZKP-friendly static quantisation brings values into small fields such as M61. A hierarchical optimizer works at three levels: model level (batch proving of LLM tokens or CNN images), primitive-operation level (it integrates known techniques such as zkCNN-style FFT convolution and zkLLM-style lookups) and circuit level (parallel sub-circuits). The circuits are proved with Polyhedra's Expander (GKR-based) engine.
record.handles_nonlinear: Lookup tables for ReLU, softmax and normalisation. Division is checked with a remainder plus a range proof. Llama-3 additionally uses temporary bit-width adjustments and piecewise lookup tables for the softmax exponent and the RMSNorm square root.
record.soundness_error: Not stated in paper.
record.trust_assumptions: Not stated in the paper. It depends on the Expander backend.
record.code_url: No zkPyTorch repository link in the paper. The Expander backend is public at https://github.com/PolyhedraZK/Expander. The Bionetta tech report (arXiv 2510.06784v2, Sec 2) says zkPyTorch 'currently it is not available for public use (as of December 2025)'.

record.paper_title: DeepProve: Verifiable End-to-End Large Language Model Inference
record.venue_year: IACR ePrint 2026/1112 (received 30 May 2026); ePrint lists 'Published elsewhere. Minor revision. CCS 2026'
record.technique: Sum-check PIOPs (layer-by-layer, GKR-like) plus logup-GKR lookup arguments, with batching across tokens. It certifies the output sequence by running inference on the concatenated input and output tokens, rather than emulating the KV cache in-circuit. There are two PCS options: BaseFold over the Goldilocks field (Ceno library, 'plausible post-quantum') or HyperKZG over BN254 (shorter proofs). A distributed prover partitions the layers into chunks.
record.handles_nonlinear: Lookup arguments (Logup GKR) for activations, Softmax and requantisation. It has specialised PIOPs for LayerNorm and RMSNorm that avoid in-circuit square roots and inverses, plus multi-head/grouped-query attention and RoPE. Activations are clamped, and residuals use mixed precision.
record.soundness_error: No numeric bound in the main text. 'We formally prove that each component is round-by-round (knowledge) sound', which the authors use to argue soundness after the Fiat-Shamir transformation (Sec 1.2; proofs in the appendices).
record.trust_assumptions: BaseFold is transparent and hash-based over Goldilocks. HyperKZG needs a pairing SRS over BN254. Fiat-Shamir is used in the non-interactive variant.
record.code_url: https://github.com/Lagrange-Labs/deep-prove (Lagrange License). The paper's [cod] link is anonymous.4open.science/r/deep-...

record.paper_title: Artemis: Efficient Commit-and-Prove SNARKs for zkML
record.technique: A CP-SNARK that binds a halo2/ZKML inference proof to an external homomorphic polynomial commitment to the weights. The committed polynomial is evaluated at a verifier challenge inside the circuit using Horner's method, via halo2's Challenge API. It works with KZG (BN254) or IPA (Pallas, no trusted setup). Baselines are No Commitment (plain ZKML arithmetization), Poseidon hashing in-circuit, Lunar CPlink, and Apollo, the authors' improved Lunar.
record.handles_nonlinear: Reuses ZKML's arithmetization (lookups).
record.soundness_error: Knowledge soundness error 'negligible in the security parameter' (appendix proofs). No numeric bit level stated.
record.trust_assumptions: KZG over BN254 needs an SRS; IPA over Pallas is transparent. The Poseidon baseline switches to BLS12-381 for Diffusion and GPT-2 because it needs more rows than BN254 allows.
record.weights_public: 7 ZKML models (mnist, resnet, dlrm, mobilenet, vgg, gpt2, diffusion) as msgpack files (360MB) in a public S3 bucket: 'aws s3 sync s3://pps-artemis-artifacts/models examples/models'. Setup params are params_kzg (64GB) and params_ipa (15GB). The README does not say whether AWS credentials are needed. None are gated.
record.notes: This is directly relevant to our Ligero/Merkle weight-commitment cost, because it measures the overhead of proving that inference used committed weights. Prover times appear only as bar charts (Figure 7, p.14, in minutes), so no exact prover numbers are given. Text: Artemis prover overhead is '1.01x-1.15x for KZG and 1.03x-1.45x for IPA' vs No Commitment. Poseidon overhead is 3.3x-17.1x (KZG) and 3.2x-17.8x (IPA). Artemis memory overhead is 1.02x-1.18x, and its verifier overhead is 1.0x-1.1x (KZG) and at most 1.2x (IPA). record.venue_year: Technical report, arXiv 2025 (arXiv:2510.06784v2, 8 Dec 2025), Rarimo / Distributed Lab
record.technique: R1CS (Circom) circuits proved with Groth16 or the authors' UltraGroth, a Groth16 variant with lookup tables. record.soundness_error: UltraGroth is proven complete, sound and zero-knowledge in the generic group model and random oracle model (Appendix A). record.paper_title: zkLLM: Zero Knowledge Proofs for Large Language Models
record.technique: Interactive zero-knowledge proof built on sumchecks over multilinear extensions for tensor operations (zkCNN/GKR-style matmul sumchecks; zkGPT notes zkLLM adopts the matmul protocol of its ref [56]). Tensors and weights are committed with Hyrax, a Pedersen-commitment variant, on BLS12-381. 'tlookup' is a parallel lookup argument for non-arithmetic tensor ops. 'zkAttn' proves softmax/attention via segmented exponent lookups. The prover is CUDA on GPU (ec-gpu BLS12-381 code). The sequential verifier parts are adapted from zkCNN and the mcl library (p.11).
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes. Activations and rescaling use tlookup, with each tlookup of size 2^16. Softmax in zkAttn uses K=5 tlookups of size 2^16, of which L=3 are least-significant segments (paper's notation, p.11). The paper reports an approximate total L1 output error of 10^-2 (p.11).
record.soundness_error: Stated only as negligible in λ (Thm 7.3 for tlookup, plus sumcheck and Pedersen/Hyrax proof-of-opening soundness, p.10). The tlookup proof sketch loses O(D/|F|) and O(ND/|F|) terms. The implementation uses BLS12-381 with '|F| ≈ 2^254' (p.10). Completeness error: honest-prover failure is 'at most O(C/|F|)', with C = total size of tensors in non-arithmetic ops (p.10). The paper assumes 'a commitment scheme that ensures λ-bit security' and |F| = Ω(2^{2λ}) (p.5). No concrete bit-security figure is given.
record.trust_assumptions: Hyrax/Pedersen commitments (discrete log), so no trusted setup (p.4). The protocol is interactive: the verifier sends random challenges in Protocol 1, and the paper does not use Fiat-Shamir. The verifier is assumed semi-honest: it reports accept/reject accurately but tries to learn the weights (p.5). There is a one-time weight-commitment phase ('Committing time' in Table 1).
record.weights_public: Llama-2-7B/13B are gated. The README requires logging in to Hugging Face, sharing contact info on the model pages, and a read access token. OPT-125M to OPT-13B (facebook/opt-*) and C4 download from Hugging Face without an account (general knowledge, not stated in the paper). The repo (MIT licence, archived Jul 10 2025) only scripts meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf and Llama-2-13b-hf; its README does not mention OPT. It was tested on A6000 and A40, recommends CUDA 12.1.0, and is GPU-only.

Hardware for Table 1: 124.5GB RAM, 12 CPU cores of an AMD EPYC 7413 (2.65 GHz), and one NVIDIA A100 SXM4 40GB GPU (p.11; the paper writes 'A100SMX4'). Workload: 'samples with the default sequence length of 2048 from the C4 dataset' (p.11; p.12 also says Table 1 uses sequence length 2048). Scaling factor is 2^16 for embeddings and parameters (p.11). All proofs verified.

Complexity (Sec 7.3, p.11):
- tlookup: prover and memory O(D) (N = O(D)); commitment size O(√D); proof size O(log D).
- zkAttn on an mn-size input: prover O(K·mn); communication and verifier O(K·√(mn)).
- For an L-layer model: O(L·t_P) prover, O(L·c) communication, O(L·t_V) verifier. The latter two can drop to O(√L·C) and O(√L·t_V) with batched commitments.

Fig. 4 (zkLLM vs zkML; the text calls GPT-2 '1.5B parameters' and says zkML OOMs beyond it, with estimated points in red) and Fig. 5 (zkAttn microbenchmarks) are plots only, with no tabulated numbers.

Their own protocol commits to 192 tensors of 64×4096.

record.paper_title: zkGPT: An Efficient Non-interactive Zero-knowledge Proof Framework for LLM Inference
record.technique: Non-interactive ZK proof built on GKR/sumcheck, based on the zkCNN code. It uses the Hyrax polynomial commitment on BN254 and is made non-interactive with Fiat-Shamir. The matmul sumcheck is optimised (grouping, exploiting small quantised value ranges and padded zeros, precomputed multiplications). Non-linear layers are proven from prover-supplied advice checked with Lasso lookups (range and exponentiation relations). Two further optimisations are 'constraint fusion' (merging adjacent rounding constraints) and 'circuit squeeze' (breaking layer dependency via committed advice to increase parallelism). Runs on CPU (C++, mcl library).
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes. GeLU, Softmax and LayerNorm are proven via advice plus range/exponentiation lookup relations (Lasso). Constraint fusion reduces GeLU rounding constraints from 2sd to sd and normalisation rounding constraints from 3s+2sd to s+sd, each 'nearly 50%' (PDF p.11).
record.soundness_error: App. B: in Case 1, via Schwartz-Zippel, the check fails to catch an error with probability at most 1/|F|. The Lasso checks pass with probability at most O((m1 + N1^{1/c} + m2 + N2)/|F|), stated as 'negligible'. The overall union bound is stated only as negligible. Implementation: 'BN254 provides around 100 bits of security' (Sec 7.1, p.2055).
record.trust_assumptions: Hyrax PCS, which is transparent (no trusted setup). Discrete log on BN254; Fiat-Shamir (random oracle). The prover range-proves committed quantised weights in [0, 2^Q], and the quantised input embedding is public.

record.paper_title: ZKTorch: Compiling ML Inference to Zero-Knowledge Proofs via Parallel Proof Accumulation
record.technique: General-purpose ZKML compiler. ONNX graphs are transpiled into a DAG of 'basic blocks': 20 are listed in Table 1, 13 of them foldable, and together they cover 61 ML layers. Each block is proved by a specialised KZG-based protocol, e.g. CQ/CQ2 lookups, CQLin/MatMul, and a Poly-IOP for the rest. A parallelised extension of the Mira accumulation scheme folds repeated basic blocks into one succinct proof. BN254 curve; CPU prover (arkworks).
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes, via lookup basic blocks (CQ for set inclusion, CQ2 for lookup tables). GeLU's 4 Mul, 1 Pow and 1 Tanh are fused into one CQ (p.10-11). Softmax is composed to prioritise accuracy (p.9). Graph-transformation rules cover GeLU, MultiHeadMatMul and RoPE (p.10). ReLU is a supported layer but not a Table 1 basic block.
record.soundness_error: All protocols are complete and knowledge sound. DAG soundness follows from a union bound: with at most 100,000 nodes, a total error e is reached by setting each node's threshold at e/10^6, and 'due to our field size, this error is negligible' (p.6). BN254 has a 254-bit prime field (p.11).
record.trust_assumptions: KZG commitments with a structured reference string from a powers-of-tau ceremony (universal trusted setup; secure if one party is honest). SDH assumption; algebraic group model; Fiat-Shamir (p.2).
record.weights_public: LLaMA-2-7B is gated (Meta licence on Hugging Face). GPT-J 6B, BERT, ResNet-50 and the other MLPerf models are publicly downloadable (general knowledge). The paper itself lists an anonymised artifact, anonymous.4open.science/r/zkt-2477 (App. A, p.15). The GitHub repo exists but is not the link given in the paper.

record.paper_title: zkPyTorch: A Hierarchical Optimized Compiler for Zero-Knowledge Machine Learning
record.technique: Compiler from PyTorch to ONNX to a DAG, then to circuits for the Expander GKR-based prover (Polyhedra). A ZKP-friendly static quantisation module (symmetric per-tensor) fits computations into small fields such as M61. Lookup tables handle non-linear ops. A hierarchical optimiser works at three levels: model level (batch verification of all LLM tokens in one circuit), primitive-operation level (reusing techniques from zkCNN/zkLLM) and circuit level (parallel sub-circuits).
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes. Lookup constraints cover ReLU, softmax and normalisation, with auxiliary witnesses (e.g. division remainders plus a proof that the remainder is smaller than the divisor; range proofs). Softmax exp and RMSNorm sqrt use temporary bit-width adjustments and piecewise lookup tables (p.6).
record.soundness_error: Not stated in the paper. The field is M61; the paper does not say whether an extension field is used for challenges.
record.trust_assumptions: Not stated in the paper. It inherits the assumptions of the Expander GKR prover.
record.weights_public: The paper says 'Llama-3' with '8 Billion' parameters but does not name the exact checkpoint. Meta Llama-3-8B is gated on Hugging Face (licence acceptance; general knowledge). VGG-16 is a CIFAR-10 model (dataset public). The zkPyTorch compiler source is not linked in the paper; only the Expander engine is referenced ([7]).

Only per-token (Llama-3) and per-image (VGG-16) proving time are reported. Proof size, verifier time, CPU model, sequence length and bit-width are not reported.

Complexity claim (Sec 3.4, p.7): batching turns about L sequential 1×H·H×W matmuls into one circuit, giving O(WH + LH) gates instead of O(LHW).

record.paper_title: NanoZK: Privacy-Preserving Verifiable Inference for Large Language Models via Layerwise Zero-Knowledge Proofs
record.venue_year: ICICS 2026 (Springer LNCS; first 12 pages of arXiv 2603.18046v2, 18 Jul 2026). Earlier version at the ICLR 2026 VerifAI workshop
record.technique: Layerwise proofs: each transformer layer (attention and MLP sub-circuits) is a separate Halo2 circuit with the IPA commitment over the Pallas field. Layers are linked by an external SHA-256 commitment chain bound to Halo2 public inputs; no hashing is done in-circuit. 16-bit fixed-point lookup tables handle softmax, GELU/SiLU and RMSNorm/LayerNorm. An optional Fisher-information-guided audit-budget triage exists, but full soundness requires verifying every layer.
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes, via 16-bit lookup tables (softmax, GELU, SiLU, RMSNorm/normalisation). Measured perplexity drift is below 10^-4 across six model/dataset combinations.
record.soundness_error: Body: 'ϵ ≈3 × 10−37 (Theorem 1)' (p.2). Theorem 1 (p.5): ϵ_total ≤ 3(L+2)·2^-λ, and at λ=128, L=32 this is ≤ 102·2^-128 ≈ 3×10^-37. App. A.2 (p.16) uses ε_IPA, ε_bind, ε_H each ≤ 2^-128 with L=12, giving ≤ 42·2^-128 ≈ 1.2×10^-37. Fisher-guided partial audits do not give full soundness.
record.trust_assumptions: No trusted setup (Halo2 IPA; transparent, pairing-free). Discrete log on Pallas; SHA-256 collision resistance; random-oracle model for the zero-knowledge simulator. Not post-quantum (p.3). The prover sees the prompt (abstract).
record.weights_public: GPT-2-small and GPT-2-medium are public on Hugging Face; TinyLLaMA-1.1B is public (general knowledge). 'LLaMA-7B (1L)' is used only for a one-layer activation-drift check. Code: 'will be released under Apache-2.0 at the URL listed in the camera-ready footnote upon ICICS publication' (App. H.8, p.41).
record.notes:
Hardware: 'single Intel Xeon CPU at 2.4 GHz with 64 GB RAM (no GPU)' (p.8). Appendix E uses a different machine, an AMD Ryzen 5950X, with different accounting; the body is authoritative (Table 10). Per App. G.1, measured proof times cover attention d≤256 and full block d≤128. The d=512, d=768 and full-block GPT-2 figures are projections from CPU MSM time, assuming a 15–30× GPU-MSM speedup.

Table 5's prior-work numbers are 'as reported': ZKML 67 min / 7.8 KB, zkLLM 15.8 s / 126 KB, zkGPT 21.8 s / 101 KB. These match zkGPT Table 3 (the caption says 32-thread CPU, and A100 for zkLLM). record.paper_title: Jolt Atlas: Verifiable Inference via Lookup Arguments in Zero Knowledge
record.technique: Adapts the Jolt lookup-centric sumcheck prover to ONNX tensor operations. Per the abstract, unlike zkVMs it does not emulate CPU instructions, although Sec 5.4 describes a CPU-trace path being replaced by tensor-level checks. It uses the HyperKZG polynomial commitment. Zero knowledge comes from BlindFold: the sumcheck verifier is encoded as R1CS and folded Nova-style with a random instance. 'Neural teleportation' shrinks lookup tables. The prover is streaming (memory-constrained), using prefix-suffix decomposition.
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes, via decomposable lookup arguments (e.g. ReLU from the sign bit, p.15). With teleportation factor τ=4, the lookup table is 'bounded by 2^16 entries (sufficient for 16-bit fixed-point activations)' (p.16).
record.soundness_error: Not stated.
record.trust_assumptions: Pairing-based HyperKZG PCS; that it requires an SRS is general knowledge and not stated in the paper. The paper lists lattice PCS as future work for post-quantum security. Fiat-Shamir challenges are used.
record.weights_public: GPT-2 (125M) is public on Hugging Face (general knowledge). The paper does not specify the checkpoint or input length.
record.notes: Hardware: 'MacBook Pro (Apple M3) with 16 GB RAM' (p.17). For GPT-2, no proof size or verifier time is reported, and the sequence length is not given. The nanoGPT ezkl numbers are taken from ezkl's published blog benchmark, not re-run.

record.paper_title: DeepProve: Verifiable End-to-End Large Language Model Inference
record.technique: Linear layers are proved with specialised sum-check PIOPs, composed GKR-style. Non-linear layers and requantisation use LogUp-GKR lookup arguments over decomposable tables, with operator fusion (delayed requantisation). The prover commits only to model parameters and lookup witnesses. It certifies the full output sequence (all generated tokens) and is made non-interactive via Fiat-Shamir, with round-by-round soundness. It is implemented in Rust on Scroll's Ceno library (Goldilocks field), with two PCS options: BaseFold, or HyperKZG on BN254. It also has a distributed (chunked) prover and an optional proof-of-non-hallucination module.
record.handles_nonlinear: Yes. Softmax, GeLU, LayerNorm, RMSNorm and requantisation use LogUp-GKR lookups over decomposable tables (pp.4-8). Over 50% of prover cost comes from activations, Softmax and requantisation (p.11).
record.soundness_error: Each PIOP is proved round-by-round (knowledge) sound. For example, the batched MatMul PIOP has rbr error max(h(1+2 log max(n_i)max(m_i))/|F|, ε_sum) (appendix, p.20). The implementation uses the 64-bit Goldilocks base field, or BN254 for HyperKZG. This check did not locate an extension field for challenges or an end-to-end concrete bit-security figure.
record.trust_assumptions: BaseFold version: hash-based, described as 'plausible post-quantum secure' (p.10). HyperKZG version: pairing-based on BN254, with shorter proofs; that it needs an SRS is general knowledge. Non-interactive via Fiat-Shamir. No input privacy (per Maverick).
record.weights_public: GPT-2 (124M) and Gemma 3 (270M) are public on Hugging Face; Gemma needs licence acceptance (general knowledge). The paper's own artifact link is anonymous.4open.science/r/deep-prove-private-C86D. The public Lagrange-Labs repo is cited by Jolt Atlas (ref [6]).
record.notes:
All experiments use 12-bit quantisation. Tables 1 (primary machine, p.10) and 2 (secondary machine, p.11) report, per model, PCS and max sequence length (64/128/256/512): context-generation time, RAM, prove time (min), verify time (s), proof size (MiB) and tokens per minute (TPM). Prove time excludes native inference. Verifier time stays under 3.2 s for GPT-2 and 3.5 s for Gemma 3; proofs are 9–43 MiB (p.11). The abstract claims 1–3.7 s verification.

Throughput: peak single-machine throughput is 174 TPM for GPT-2 (175 TPM at seq. 256) on the secondary machine, and 86 TPM for Gemma 3. Simulated distributed throughput with 16 workers reaches 1855 TPM (Table 6).

Table 3 (p.12) converts baselines to TPM: zkGPT 2.75 TPM and ZKTorch GPT-J 0.09 TPM. It excludes zkLLM as GPU-only.

It is the only GPT-2 system in this family whose paper states the sequence length.

Maverick (arXiv 2609.10264v1): a Freivalds-style check with sparse challenges over linear-code encodings, with information-theoretic soundness for matrix-vector multiplication delegation. It is technically closest to our batched-Freivalds defence. It benchmarks only Qwen3-4B, in verification-only mode: 531.6 ms end-to-end including inference, 45.1 ms client verification, 36.08 MB communication, 8-token prompt (p.15). It is not catalogued as a system here.
